body.purpose: All paragraph content in Arabic. 1.8 line-height is non-negotiable for Arabic readability.

label.purpose: Navigation items, badge text, meta fields. No all-caps at this scale.

shadows.name: amber-avatar-glow

motion.name: fade-in

motion.name: avatar-frame-hover

narrative.overview:
A portfolio that earns trust through execution quality, not declaration. The visual system is confident without being loud — amber warmth set against a warm-stone canvas, generous Arabic line-heights that respect the letterform, minimal decorative noise. Every element serves evidence: evidence of craft, reliability, and five-plus years of deliberate frontend engineering.

Arabic-first is not a localization layer but the design foundation. Line-height begins at 1.8, base font size scales to 1.125rem, and Tajawal shapes every reading experience from the opening glyph. RTL is the grid direction, not a mirror.

This system explicitly rejects the SaaS gradient template, the "passionate developer" portfolio trope, and the 2026 cream/warm-neutral AI reflex.
keyCharacteristics: Amber as mark, not as mood — appears on three brand moments per page, maximum
Arabic readability baked into the type scale, not retrofitted
Staggered motion with purpose — reveal sequences for list items, not uniform entrance reflex
Surfaces layered by tone (base / elevated / muted), shadows reserved for state

rules.name: The Honey Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber appears on three brand moments maximum per screen: the designer's name, one focal CTA, one availability badge. Amber is a signature, not a fill color. If a fourth amber element appears, remove one.

rules.name: The Stone Canvas Rule
rules.body: The warm-neutral danger zone (cream, sand, linen, parchment) is avoided. Stone-50 reads as near-white, not warm beige — its character comes from amber context, not from boosted background chroma.

rules.name: The Arabic Baseline Rule
rules.body: Body font size is 1.125rem. Line-height is 1.8. These are not adjustable defaults — Arabic letterforms fail readability at Latin-designed baselines.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Rubik for headings and display; Tajawal for Arabic body. Monospace is scoped to blog content rendering only — not a global third family.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest carry no shadow. A new shadow is permitted only if it communicates a specific state (stickiness, hover) or belongs to an existing metaphor (polaroid).

dos: Do apply .text-amber only to the designer's name and one or two other focal brand moments per screen.
Do keep body line-height at 1.8 and base font size at 1.125rem everywhere Arabic text appears.
Do use rounded-full exclusively for pills (nav, availability badge) and rounded-sm (0.5rem) for interactive controls.
Do stagger animation-delay increments on list items to reflect reading order — 0.1s steps.
Do check contrast before any amber text on light surface. Honey Light (#fbbf24) fails 4.5:1 against white; use Honey Deep (#d97706) for body-scale text in light mode.
Do keep hero atmospheric amber (mesh, glow) at 14–30% opacity maximum.
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient). .text-amber is the committed replacement.
Don't replicate the SaaS landing template: hero → stats block → icon-grid features → testimonials → CTA.
Don't use the 'passionate developer' portfolio structure: name in gradient, generic tagline, project card grid with hover-glow.
Don't use cream, sand, linen, or warm-tinted near-white as a page background.
Don't apply entrance animations to every section. The stagger pattern belongs to list items within a section.
Don't place border-left or border-right > 1px as a colored stripe on UI components.
Don't override the Arabic baseline: 1.125rem body and 1.8 line-height are non-negotiable.
